chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), regarding

the man who dies and upon him are prayers or fasting. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The one closest to the people in inheritance should make it up for him.' I said: 'And if the one closest to him is a woman?' So he is a woman?' He said: 'No, except for the men.'

key_terms.أَوْلَى النَّاسِ بِمِيرَاثِهِ: The one closest to him in inheritance

ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for making up the prayers and fasts of a deceased person according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the mechanism of qada (making up) for missed prayers and fasts, establishing that the closest male heir assumes the responsibility for the deceased's outstanding devotional debts. While Shia jurisprudence generally permits women to perform qada for themselves, this specific narration highlights a distinct juristic opinion restricting the代理 role for others to males, reflecting the interplay between inheritance proximity and gender in ritual obligations. This ruling underscores the concept of 'debt to God' being settled by the heir's physical performance, linking spiritual accountability with familial lineage.
